title: Which ten digits should stay to make the largest number?
description: Ten digits are struck out of a twenty digit number made of the digits one to five written four times. The biggest digit is brought to the front again and again, within the ten strikes allowed. The strikes are counted at the end.
teaching_notes: One idea: the leftmost digit matters most, so strike out the small digits in front of each big digit while the strikes last. Watch for students who strike out the smallest digits anywhere instead of working from the left.

source: Strike out 10 digits from the number 12345123451234512345 so that the remaining number is as large as possible.
video_script.why: The child knows that the leftmost digits decide how big a number is, and now uses that to choose which digits to keep.
video_script.substitution: Work from the left; strike out the small digits in front of the biggest digit that can be reached, while strikes remain.
video_script.anchor: a twenty digit number made of the digits one to five written four times, in a long row of boxes
video_script.payoff_line: Strike out the small digits in front of each big digit while the strikes last

final_answer.spoken: five, five, three, four, five, one, two, three, four, five

maths_rules: the number has 20 digits; striking out 10 leaves 10
first digit: the first 5 is 4 digits in, so strike out 1 2 3 4 (4 strikes)
second digit: the next 5 is 4 digits further on, so strike out 1 2 3 4 (4 more strikes, 8 in all)
a third 5 needs 4 more strikes, giving 12, too many; strike out 1 2 (10 in all) so that 3 comes next
a 4 after the two 5s would need 3 more strikes, giving 11, too many
video_script.design: One idea: the leftmost digit matters most. The twenty digit row stays in the anchor band; the working band shows the strikes in order. No hard clear.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Here is a number made of the digits one to five, written four times.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>We must strike out ten of its digits.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Which digits should stay, so that the number left is as large as possible?

beats.on_screen: the anchor holds still; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: cards: 20 digits - 10 struck = 10 digits left; the leftmost digit matters most; striking a digit pulls later digits forward

marks.m1: the card 20 digits - 10 struck = 10 digits left appears
marks.m2: the card the leftmost digit matters most appears
marks.m3: a digit is struck out and the digits after it slide forward

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Twenty digits less ten struck out leaves ten digits.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Among ten digit numbers, the one with the biggest leftmost digit is the largest.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Striking a digit out pulls the digits after it forward.

marks.m1: the given line is written in the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, the digits one to five written four times, and ten digits to strike out.

beats.on_screen: To find: the largest number that remains

marks.m1: the find line is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find the largest number that remains.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: first digit as big as possible, 5; strike 1 2 3 4 before the first 5 (4 strikes used)

marks.m2: the digits 1 2 3 4 before it are struck out

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, the first digit should be as big as possible, which is five.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Strike out the four digits one, two, three, four in front of the first five.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>That uses four strikes.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: second digit 5 again; strike 1 2 3 4 before the next 5 (4 more strikes, 8 used)

marks.m2: the digits 1 2 3 4 before it are struck out

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, the second digit should also be five.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The next five is four digits away, so strike out one, two, three, four again.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>That makes eight strikes in all.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 2 strikes remain; a third 5 needs 4 more, too many; strike 1 2 so that 3 comes next; keep the rest

marks.m2: the third 5 is shown four digits away and crossed with the word too far
marks.m3: the digits 1 and 2 are struck out and 3 is lit
marks.m4: the rest of the digits are lit as kept

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, two strikes remain.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>A third five is too far away, since it needs four more strikes.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Strike out one and two, so that three comes next.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Then keep all the rest of the digits.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check: 4 + 4 + 2 = 10 strikes, 10 digits remain; a 4 after the two 5s needs 3 more strikes, 11 in all, too many

marks.m3: a 4 after the two 5s is shown needing 3 more strikes, with the word too many

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, check the count.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Four, four and two strikes make ten, and ten digits remain.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>A four straight after the two fives would need three strikes more, which is too many.

marks.m2: the ten digits are underlined one by one

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Strike out the small digits in front of each big digit while the strikes last.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The largest number left is five, five, three, four, five, one, two, three, four, five.
